# CalcBloc Tax Tables — 2026 income tax and social security data for 41 countries

[![Licence: CC BY 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-CC%20BY%204.0-blue.svg)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) [![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.24153625.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24153625)

Free, machine-readable **income tax tables** and **social security contribution rates** for 41 countries, compiled by [CalcBloc](https://calcbloc.com/?utm_source=calcbloc-data&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=itmarkerz-oss) from official government sources. Each table covers one country and tax year (the 2026 and 2026-27 tax years) and lists the **tax brackets**, personal allowances and credits, employee and employer contributions with their ceilings, and other payroll figures, with regional tables for states, provinces and cantons where they set their own rates.

Every row states its official source URL, the date it was retrieved and a review status, so each figure can be traced back to the government page it came from. The data is the same that powers the tax-table pages and calculators on [calcbloc.com](https://calcbloc.com/?utm_source=calcbloc-data&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=itmarkerz-oss) and the [CalcBloc API](https://calcbloc.com/developers?utm_source=calcbloc-data&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=itmarkerz-oss).

CalcBloc is a product of [itmarkerz technologies](https://itmarkerz.co.in/?utm_source=calcbloc-data&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=itmarkerz-oss).

**At a glance:** 41 countries · 246 tables (42 national, 204 regional) · 11,570 rows · 1,407 official sources · last verified 2026-11-13 · CSV and JSON · CC BY 4.0

## What the tables contain

- **Income tax brackets** (marginal rates and band limits), including state, provincial, cantonal or regional scales where they exist
- **Allowances, credits and deductions** that set the tax-free amount (personal allowance, basic exemption, tax credits)
- **Social security contribution rates** for employees and employers: pension, health, unemployment and other insurances, with contribution ceilings and thresholds
- **Employer payroll costs**: payroll taxes, levies and employer-only contributions
- **Other figures** shown on the country's calcbloc.com tax-table page, for example VAT, corporation tax or minimum-wage rows

Rates are decimal fractions (0.2 = 20%) and money amounts are in the country's currency. The [data dictionary](dist/DATA_DICTIONARY.md) describes every column.

Regional tables (for example Canada: Ontario) hold only the regional figures; combine them with the national table of the same year. They are listed in [dist/TABLES.md](dist/TABLES.md) with their sources, and in [dist/tables-summary.csv](dist/tables-summary.csv).

### Pending countries

Belgium is not included yet: held until the 2026 federal income-tax scale is confirmed against the official FPS Finance publication. It will be added as soon as its tables are complete.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`dist/calcbloc-tax-tables-all.csv`](dist/calcbloc-tax-tables-all.csv) | Every row of every table in one long-format CSV (11,570 rows) |
| [`dist/calcbloc-tax-tables-all.json`](dist/calcbloc-tax-tables-all.json) | The same rows as JSON, with dataset metadata |
| `dist/csv/<country>/<year>.csv` | One CSV per national table, e.g. [`dist/csv/uk/2026-27.csv`](dist/csv/uk/2026-27.csv) |
| `dist/csv/<country>/<year>/<region>.csv` | One CSV per regional table |
| `dist/json/...` | The same tables as JSON, with the table's sources, status and attribution |
| [`dist/tables-summary.csv`](dist/tables-summary.csv) / [`.json`](dist/tables-summary.json) | One row per table: tax year, last-verified date, row counts, official source URLs, page and API links |
| [`dist/TABLES.md`](dist/TABLES.md) | The same summary as a readable list, with the official sources per country |
| [`dist/DATA_DICTIONARY.md`](dist/DATA_DICTIONARY.md) | Every column, unit and status value explained |
| [`dist/datapackage.json`](dist/datapackage.json) | [Frictionless Data Package](https://datapackage.org/) descriptor with the field schema |
| `tables/` | The source files as exported from calcbloc.com (the API's JSON shape) plus `manifest.json` |

All CSV files share one set of columns, so any of them can be appended to the combined file. They are UTF-8 with a header row and CRLF line endings.

## How to use the data

**Download a CSV** from the links above, or load it straight from GitHub. In Python with pandas:

```python
import pandas as pd

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itmarkerz/calcbloc-data/main/dist/calcbloc-tax-tables-all.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(url, dtype={"tax_year": str, "region_code": str})

# United Kingdom, 2026-27: Income Tax bands: England and Northern Ireland
bands = df[(df.country == "uk") & (df.tax_year == "2026-27") & df.region_code.isna() & (df.section_id == "income-tax-england")]
print(bands[["label", "from", "to", "rate"]])
```

```js
const res = await fetch("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itmarkerz/calcbloc-data/main/dist/json/uk/2026-27.json");
const table = await res.json();
console.log(table.country_name, table.tax_year, table.last_verified, table.rows.length, "rows");
```

It works without a key for 50 requests a day per IP address, on every endpoint; when that runs out, add a [free API key](https://calcbloc.com/developers/keys?utm_source=calcbloc-data&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=itmarkerz-oss) for 5,000 a day, sent in the `X-API-Key` header:

```sh
curl https://calcbloc.com/api/v1/tax-tables/uk/2026-27
curl "https://calcbloc.com/api/v1/tax-tables/canada/2026?region=on&format=csv"
```

## Status values and verification

Each row has a `status`:

- `verified`: The figure was checked against the official source given in source_url on the retrieved_at date.
- `under_review`: The row belongs to a section that is flagged for manual re-verification: a figure in it rests on a copy of the official page rather than the page itself, a later re-check could not reproduce it, or the underlying record is not yet marked verified. The whole section is flagged, so most rows in it are usually correct. Confirm the figure against source_url before relying on it; calcbloc.com marks the same sections as under review.
- `not_applicable`: A sourced "does not apply" row: the source confirms that the item does not exist in that jurisdiction (for example a state with no labour welfare fund, or a country with no statutory minimum wage). value then holds a short explanation.

193 of the 11,570 rows are currently `under_review`. They are kept in the dataset, with their status, so every table is complete; filter on `status` if you need checked figures only. Tables with figures under review say so on their calcbloc.com page too.

## How updates work

The tables are maintained in the calcbloc.com code base, where every figure is entered from an official source together with its URL and retrieval date. This repository holds an export of that data and generates every file from it:

1. `npm run sync` runs the site's exporter ([`scripts/sync-tables.mjs`](scripts/sync-tables.mjs)) and refreshes `tables/` (one JSON file per country, tax year and region, plus `manifest.json`).
2. `npm run build` ([`scripts/build.mjs`](scripts/build.mjs)) regenerates `dist/`, this README, the dataset cards and the citation files from `tables/`.
3. `npm test` checks that every row has a source URL and retrieval date, that the CSV and JSON files hold the same rows, and that the files match the manifest.

A new tax year or a corrected figure is therefore one change: sync, build, test, commit. The per-row `retrieved_at` dates and the git history show what changed and when; the [calcbloc.com data changelog](https://calcbloc.com/data/changelog?utm_source=calcbloc-data&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=itmarkerz-oss) lists updates to the underlying datasets. Requires Node.js 22 or later; there are no dependencies to install.
